priceVsEarnings.title: Price vs Earnings
priceVsEarnings.subtitle: Whether profit growth has kept up with the share price
priceVsEarnings.methodology: Both series are per share — price and diluted EPS — and both are rebased to 100 at the start of the window, so they share one scale. The vertical gap between the lines is exactly the change in the P/E multiple since the base date. A second axis would hide an undeclared multiple in the ratio between the two scales. EPS is trailing twelve months, mapped to the date it was actually filed.
priceVsEarnings.logHint: Logarithmic scale — equal vertical distances mean equal percentage moves. Useful when one series grows many times over.
priceVsEarnings.baseShifted: base = first quarter with positive EPS in the window

problem.title: Our Goal
problem.text: To give the individual investor easy, structured, and transparent access to corporate financial statements. By automating the extraction of complex SEC reports, we free up your time for what really matters: value analysis.

organization.title: The Bullocracy
organization.text: BullValue is built by The Bullocracy, an organization of young students seeking to democratize access to knowledge about Politics, Economics, and Investments. To achieve this, they create content on social media, from YouTube to TikTok, fostering a space for our community to write articles and opinions to be published online, on the website thebullocracy.com, where they stimulate free debate and financial literacy.

compound.title: Compound Interest
compound.subtitle: Compound interest calculator to simulate your wealth growth.

tooltips.initialAmount: The capital you have available to allocate at the start of the simulation.
tooltips.monthlyContribution: The amount you plan to add regularly. Small consistent contributions maximize the exponential effect of compound interest.
tooltips.contribFreq: The frequency with which you will add new funds to the investment.
tooltips.contribTiming: Investing at the beginning of the period maximizes returns, since the capital spends more time in the market.
tooltips.years: The time horizon. Time is the mathematical variable with the greatest impact on the growth of Compound Interest.
tooltips.preset: Choose a fixed rate or a benchmark index. Indices auto-fill the rate with that market's historical average annualized return (CAGR) for the chosen window — price change only, excluding dividends.
tooltips.lookback: Sets the historical window used to estimate the index's annualized average return.
tooltips.interestRate: The projected annual return. Auto-filled with the historical CAGR when you pick a benchmark index; edit it freely for your own scenario.
tooltips.compound: The frequency with which the investment generates interest on accumulated profits. Stock market return is generally modeled with Annual compounding.

compound.disclaimer: Simulation for educational purposes only. Index returns are historical averages (price change, excluding dividends) and do not guarantee future results. This is not financial advice.

yieldCurve.description: The spread between 10-year and 2-year yields. An inverted curve (below zero) has historically been the market's most reliable recession warning.

fedFunds.title: Federal Funds Rate
fedFunds.description: The benchmark interest rate set by the Federal Reserve. It governs how easily money flows through the entire economy, driving cycles of expansion or contraction.

cpi.title: Inflation (CPI YoY)
cpi.description: The year-over-year percentage change in the Consumer Price Index. High inflation erodes purchasing power and forces central banks to raise rates, choking the economy.

gdp.title: GDP Growth (Real GDP YoY)
gdp.description: Real growth of the United States Gross Domestic Product. The definitive thermometer of the real economy.

unemployment.title: Unemployment Rate (US)
unemployment.description: The percentage of the US labor force that is unemployed. Rapid increases (the Sahm Rule) signal imminent danger.

vix.title: Volatility (VIX)
vix.description: The famous 'Fear Index'. It measures the market's expectation of 30-day volatility. Readings above 30 indicate widespread panic.

dcfModelo.vazio: Pick a company to open the model. Assumptions come prefilled from analyst consensus and history, and you can change everything.
dcfModelo.reporAjuda: Go back to the initial assumptions (consensus and history). Your changes for this company are removed from this browser.
dcfModelo.fontes: Balance sheet as of {balanco} · Risk-free rate (US 10-year Treasury) as of {rf} · {n} years of analyst consensus · Source: BullValue

linhas.capexLiquidoNota: Capex minus D&A: investment above maintenance
linhas.sbcNota: Already included in EBIT as an expense
linhas.fracaoNota: In year 1 only the part of the fiscal year still ahead counts

dcfModelo.historicoAjuda: The last 10 actual years, as corrected by BullValue, with the ratios that anchor the assumptions.
dcfModelo.projecoesAjuda: Projected income statement and the FCFF build: NOPAT + D&A − capex − increase in working capital. Negative values in parentheses.

schedules.receitaAjuda: Revenue projected from each year's growth. The first years come from analyst consensus.
schedules.custosAjuda: Gross margin sets cost of revenue (used for inventory and payable days). EBIT margin sets operating income.
schedules.capexAjuda: Investment and amortization as % of revenue. Capex well above D&A for a long time means the company is still growing its asset base.
schedules.fundoManeioAjuda: Receivables, inventory, payables and deferred revenue projected by days. Deferred revenue (billed in advance) reduces working capital, which matters for subscription businesses. An increase in working capital consumes cash.
schedules.impostosAjuda: Effective rate applied to EBIT (operating tax, as if the company had no debt).
schedules.inputsNota: Drivers in blue come from Assumptions (the inputs). Schedules only calculate, year by year; to change a value, go to Assumptions.
schedules.inputsNotaNova: Blue rows are the inputs: click one to open the panel with historical data, analyst consensus and the controls.

pressupostos.operacionaisAjuda: The model inputs, in one place (the FMVA "blue cells"). For each driver: the Year 1 value, the final-year value and the path between them. "By year" opens the row to fine-tune specific years. Schedules only calculate from here.
pressupostos.erpAjuda: Required return on equities above the risk-free rate
pressupostos.gAjuda: Growth forever after the last year; should not exceed the risk-free rate
pressupostos.multiploAjuda: Starts from the current multiple, capped at 6x–20x
pressupostos.waccManualAjuda: Leave empty to use the CAPM WACC
pressupostos.igualY1Ajuda: Constant: same as Year 1. Click to switch to Linear.
pressupostos.customAjuda: Edited year by year. Pick Constant or Linear to go back to a simple path.
pressupostos.consensoAjuda: Years 1 to 3 from analyst consensus, then a straight-line fade to the final year.

avaliacao.nota: Discounted from today. {f} of year 1 counts: the part of the fiscal year after the balance sheet date used in the bridge (earlier flows are already in cash and debt). Terminal value is discounted from the end of the last year.

avisos.pesoTerminal: Terminal value is {pct} of enterprise value: the result depends heavily on long-term assumptions. Consider a longer horizon.
avisos.gAcimaRf: Perpetual growth is above the risk-free rate: a company cannot outgrow the economy forever.
avisos.divergencia: The two methods diverge: the exit multiple implies {g} perpetual growth, and Gordon implies a {mult} multiple. One of the assumptions may be unrealistic.

erros.carregar: Could not load the data. Please try again.
erros.naoEncontrada: Not enough history for the model.
erros.WACC_MENOR_QUE_G: WACC must be above perpetual growth for the Gordon terminal value to make sense. Raise WACC, lower growth or use the exit multiple.
erros.SEM_ACOES: No share count to compute value per share.

receita.outrosNota: Revenue not attributed to any segment (eliminations, unallocated). In the projection it keeps its weight relative to the segments.
receita.segmentosAjuda: Revenue is the sum of the segments. Each segment starts from its 3-year CAGR, calibrated so that Year 1 total matches consensus, and fades to the final year. Compare the 'Revenue growth' row with consensus.
receita.semSegmentos: This company has no verified segments in BullValue (or reports only one): the Revenue Build uses total growth.

multiplo.nota: Weekly line, using the trailing 12-month EBITDA known at each date. An exit multiple well above the median assumes the market keeps paying more than it did in the past.

painel.ebitAjustado: Consensus EBIT may include non-operating gains; the suggested margin is capped to the historical range ±5 pp.
painel.taxaLegal: US reference: 21% federal, about 25% including state taxes. The effective rate can be lower due to tax credits and foreign profits.
painel.paresNota: Median of the companies in the same industry on BullValue, in each one's latest fiscal year.

sensibilidade.semModelo: There is no sensitivity without a valid model: fix the Valuation tab first.

waccG.ajuda: Value per share when WACC and terminal growth change. The centre is your model; green is above the current price, red below. Empty cells: WACC does not exceed growth.

crescMargem.ajuda: Value per share when percentage points are added to revenue growth and EBIT margin in every projected year. The centre is your model.

cenarios.ajuda: Each scenario is the full model with its own assumptions: pick it in the Scenario switch and edit it in Schedules and Valuation. The expected value is weighted by your probabilities.
cenarios.somaAviso: The probabilities add up to {soma}, not 100%: the expected value uses them proportionally.
cenarios.derivarAjuda: Restart this scenario from the current Base (±3 pp growth and margin, ±2x multiple, ±0.5 pp g). Discards this scenario’s edits.

football.ajuda: The value-per-share range of each analysis, against the current price and your model's value.

waccMultiplo.ajuda: Value per share as WACC and the exit EV/EBITDA multiple change. The centre is your model; green above the current price, red below.

sensibilidade.doCenario: Sensitivity of the {cenario} case (the selected one)

cenario.ajuda: Each scenario has its own assumptions. Schedules and Valuation edit the selected scenario.

macro.linha: Inflation (CPI) {cpi} + real GDP {pib} ≈ nominal GDP {nominal}. 10-year risk-free rate {rf}. Your terminal growth: {g}.
macro.gAcima: Terminal growth is above current US nominal GDP: no company outgrows the economy forever.
macro.nota: US year-over-year change up to {data}. An anchor, not a rule: long-run growth tends to sit between inflation and nominal GDP.

resumo.ajuda: The result of the {cenario} scenario, the three scenarios and the assumptions that matter most. The PDF and the Excel file carry the same content.
resumo.teseAjuda: Your reasoning, in free text. It is saved in this browser with the rest of the draft and goes into the PDF and the Excel file.
resumo.tesePlaceholder: Why these assumptions? What would change your mind?
resumo.erroExportar: Could not export. Please try again.

versoes.ajuda: Save the model to your account, with the thesis, and come back to it later. Every save is a new version; an earlier one is never overwritten.
versoes.nomePlaceholder: Version name (optional): e.g. after Q2 results
versoes.erroGuardar: Could not save. Please try again.
versoes.vazio: You haven't saved any version of this company yet.
versoes.confirmarCarregar: Opening v{n} replaces this browser's current draft. Continue?
versoes.confirmarApagar: Delete v{n}? This cannot be undone.

financeira.intro: Banks, insurers and brokers are valued by residual income: how much equity earns above what it costs (ROE − Ke). Equity value = current book equity + present value of future excess returns. There is no debt bridge: it is already equity value.
financeira.semDados: Not enough equity or history for this model.
financeira.ke: Cost of equity (Ke) = risk-free rate + beta × equity risk premium = {ke}

pressupostos.ajuda: ROE moves in a straight line from year 1 to the last year; the terminal value uses the final ROE. Starting values are the 3-year median.
pressupostos.roeInicialAjuda: Net income over opening shareholders' equity.
pressupostos.roeFinalAjuda: By default, half of the excess over Ke persists: the edge fades, it does not vanish.
pressupostos.payoutAjuda: Share of earnings distributed. The rest stays in equity and grows the balance sheet.
pressupostos.gAjuda: By default, no higher than what the final ROE and the payout can fund.

financeira.projecaoAjuda: Year 1 is the 12 months after the {data} balance sheet; flows are discounted at the end of each year. Equity is the group's, including preferred shares.

ponte.somaVp: Sum of PV of residual income
ponte.pesoTerminal: Terminal value as % of equity value

sensibilidade.ajuda: Value per share when the cost of equity and the final ROE change. The centre is your model.

avisos.gInsustentavel: Terminal growth of {g} is above what the final ROE and payout fund ({s}): the balance sheet cannot grow that fast without new capital.
avisos.roeAlto: An ROE above 30% is rare and short-lived: check it is not inflated by buybacks or an exceptional year.

erros.KE_MENOR_QUE_G: The cost of equity must exceed terminal growth. Lower growth or raise beta.
erros.SEM_ACOES: No share count to compute the value per share.

dcfSimples.vazio: Pick a company. The simple DCF projects FCF per share or EPS in three scenarios and tells you how much you can pay today to earn the return you want.
dcfSimples.reporAjuda: Go back to the initial scenarios (consensus and history).
dcfSimples.anoSaida: multiple the stock trades at in year {n}
dcfSimples.fairValueAjuda: the most you can pay today to earn {r} a year
dcfSimples.cagrAjuda: annual return if you buy at {p}
dcfSimples.cagrCor: Green if ≥ the desired return ({r}), red if below.
dcfSimples.graficoAjuda: Bars: actual values per year. Lines: the three scenarios from the TTM value.
